response.justification: The candidate is an experienced full-stack/web software developer with strong general engineering skills, but the role requires deep hardware expertise: SoC/IP modeling, AI accelerator performance analysis, GPU architecture, and hardware-software co-design. Aside from some low-latency systems work with DLang and a brief C/C++ stint at National Instruments, the resume shows no experience in computer architecture, deep-learning workload optimization, or chip design. This is a fundamental domain mismatch for a Principal Performance Architect position.
strengths: 15+ years of broad software engineering experience, meeting the years-of-experience bar
Some systems-level experience: low-latency DLang services, async I/O, and C/C++ work at National Instruments
Strong engineering practices (TDD, CI/CD) and open-source contributions demonstrating initiative
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, computer architecture, or hardware-software co-design experience
No AI/deep-learning workload, GPU, or SIMD/MIMD accelerator background
Career trajectory is web/full-stack product development, far from principal-level performance architecture

key_factors.factor: No AI accelerator or DL workload optimization background
General seniority and systems programming exposure
